question: The Food Corporation of India procures foodgrains from the farmers at the government announced __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**minimum support price.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Food Corporation of India **procures foodgrains from the **farmers** at the government announced **minimum support price.**
 
• The minimum support price is the price at which the government procures crops from the farmers to ensure that they get a** fair price** for their produce.
 
• The **Food Corporation of India** is the nodal agency.
 
• The minimum support price is announced by the government **every year before the sowing **season to ensure that farmers are incentivized to grow crops.
 
• The minimum support price is calculated based on factors such as the **cost of production, market price trends, **and other factors to ensure that farmers get a fair price for their produce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maximum Retail Price** is the **maximum price** at which a product can be **sold to the end consumer**.

 
 
• It is usually fixed by the manufacturer or the government to prevent retailers from **overcharging customers.**
 
 
 
• **Competitive Price** is the price at which a product is** sold in the market** based on the demand and supply dynamics.
 
 
• It is usually determined by the **market forces** and can fluctuate based on various factors such as **competition, seasonality, etc.**
 
 
 
• **Discounted Price** is the price at which a product is **sold at a lower price** than the market price.
 
 
• It is usually offered as a promotional offer or during a **sale to attract customers**.
 
• However, it is **no**t a sustainable pricing strategy in the long run.
